name: Lough Derg

attributes.attribute: monster or serpent defeated by Saint Patrick
said to have his palace at the Galway lake

sources: Dames, Michael. Mythic Ireland. London: Thames and Hudson, 1992, pp. 22 ff.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Lough Derg is a lake in County Donegal, Ireland. Legend says a great monster or serpent called Caoranach once lived there. Saint Patrick overcame the creature, and its blood stained the water a dark red, which gave the lake its name, dark red lake. A second lake of the same name lies in County Galway. There the great magician Bodb Derg of the Tuatha De Danann was said to have his palace. Since Ireland became Christian, the Donegal lake has become Ireland's chief place of pilgrimage, built around Saint Patrick's Purgatory.

okr.objective: Document Lough Derg as a Donegal lake tied to Saint Patrick and a Galway lake tied to Bodb Derg.
key_results: Caoranach was a monster or serpent defeated by Saint Patrick
